text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romanian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Prices for fuel will increase only if the leu's exchange rate would exceed 8,500 to the dollar, the Romanian Oil Company said.
- The first stage in restructuring Romania's industrial sectors might trigger labour unrest, the paper says.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- The local leu currency continued its upward trend and people queued at retail shops to exchange their dollars into lei to make deposits at commercial banks which offer attractive interest rates.
- The government decided to use 550,000 tonnes of wheat from the state reserves to meet demand until the new wheat harvest, expected to be completed by July.
- Butan Gas Romania SAwill invest $6.0 million to upgrade LPG bottles used by the population.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- The king is finally back from exile, the newspaper says.
- Farming unions asked the government ro continue to subsidise the spring farm works, worth a total of 7.2 billion lei.
- International adoptions have allegedly brought illegal gains worth hundreds of thousand dollars, the newspaper says.
- Prosecutors started investigations into alleged illegal court rulings on adoptions. Prosecutors said many of the files related to those adoptions had disappered from the archives.
ADEVARUL
- Former tennis star Ilie Nastase and gymnast Nadia Comaneci will lobby for Romania in the United States and Germany.
- The government gives 13,500 lei monthly compensations to all state employees for recent bread price hikes.

- Romania's exiled King Michael, who will return to his country on Friday, might "play his last political role" the paper says in editorial. Michael is expected to lobby for Romania's integration into NATO.

- The main opposition Party of Social Democracy plans to introduce a motion in parliament to protest against the government moves to cut subsidies to the farming sector. The motion cannot lead to a reshuffle.
- Romania ranks first among European countries when it comes to HIV-infected children, AIDS children, tuberculosis and abortion cases, health ministry data show.
CURIERUL NATIONAL

- National Liberal Party (PNL) -- a member of the ruling coalition -- asked trade unions to support politicians' efforts to integrate Romania into NATO. ($= 7,744 lei) -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
